title: Network Gateway High-Throughput Packet Filter Prefix Trie
problem_statement:
A carrier-grade software-defined network (SDN) gateway inspects packet protocol strings using a custom-built 26-ary prefix tree (Trie). The trie must support dynamic insertion of domain patterns, exact keyword lookup, and prefix-matching for wildcard firewall rules.

Implement the Trie data structure from scratch and process Q operations on an initially empty Trie:
- `1 word`: Insert the lowercase string `word` into the trie.
- `2 word`: Search for the exact string `word`. Print `true` if it exists as a complete word, otherwise print `false`.
- `3 prefix`: Check if there is any previously inserted word that starts with the given string `prefix`. Print `true` if such a prefix exists, otherwise print `false`.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer Q, the number of operations.
The following Q lines each contain an operation type (1, 2, or 3) followed by a string argument.
output_format: For each operation of type 2 or 3, print `true` or `false` on a new line.
constraints:
1 <= Q <= 10^5
1 <= |word|, |prefix| <= 100
Strings consist of lowercase English letters.
explanation:
- Insert "apple".
- Search "apple": exists -> true.
- Search "app": "app" was not inserted as a complete word -> false.
- StartsWith "app": "apple" starts with "app" -> true.
- Insert "app".

test_cases.input:
6
1 fire
1 firewall
2 fire
2 wire
3 fir
3 wir

edge_cases.explanation: Queries on empty trie return false.

title: Deep Space Telemetry Keyword Shortest Unique Prefix Resolution
problem_statement:
An interplanetary uplink channel possesses restricted bandwidth. To compress transmission tokens, every telecommand keyword in an authorization dictionary of N distinct words must be mapped to its shortest unique prefix that unambiguously distinguishes it from all other words in the dictionary.

Construct a Trie where each node records the frequency of words traversing through it. For each word in the input list in original order, determine the shortest prefix that reaches a node with frequency 1 (or the complete word if no prefix has frequency 1).

Print the shortest unique prefix for each word, separated by a single space.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of words.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing the words.
output_format: Print the N shortest unique prefixes in the order of the input words, separated by a single space.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^4
1 <= |word| <= 100
Total characters <= 10^5
All words are lowercase English letters and pairwise distinct.
explanation:
- "zebra": prefix "z" appears in no other word -> "z"
- "dog": prefix "d" shared with duck and dove, "do" shared with dove, "dog" is unique -> "dog"
- "duck": prefix "d" shared, "du" is unique -> "du"
- "dove": prefix "do" shared with dog, "dov" is unique -> "dov"

edge_cases.explanation: One word is prefix of another: 'ab' needs both characters, 'a' needs 'a'.

title: Continuous Unsegmented Telemetry Stream Lexicon Decomposition
problem_statement:
An automated deep-space transmission decoder receives a contiguous, unsegmented string S of hexadecimal/alphabetic telemetry tokens without delimiter spaces. An authorized lexicon of N dictionary words is known.

Using a Trie to index the dictionary words and dynamic programming with prefix lookahead, determine if the contiguous stream S can be completely segmented into a sequence of one or more valid dictionary words.

Print 1 if the string can be fully decomposed into dictionary words, otherwise print 0.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of words in the dictionary.
The second line contains N space-separated dictionary words.
The third line contains the unsegmented query string S.
output_format: Print 1 if S can be segmented into dictionary words, otherwise print 0.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= |word| <= 50
1 <= |S| <= 1000
All strings consist of lowercase English letters.
sample_input:
12
i like sam sung samsung mobile ice cream icecream man go mango
ilikesamsung
explanation: The string "ilikesamsung" can be segmented as "i like sam sung" or "i like samsung", all of which are valid dictionary words.

test_cases.input:
12
i like sam sung samsung mobile ice cream icecream man go mango
ilikesamsung

5
apple banana orange grape pear
applepineapple

edge_cases.explanation: Target matches single dictionary word exactly.
Target contains characters not present in dictionary.

title: Distributed Document Clustering: Anagram Equivalent Grouping
problem_statement:
A distributed web crawler indexes N document keywords. Words that are anagrams of one another (contain identical character frequencies) share equivalent semantic indices and must be clustered together.

Given an array of N words:
1. Group all words that are mutual anagrams together.
2. Within each anagram group, sort the words in lexicographical (alphabetical) order.
3. Sort the distinct groups in lexicographical order by their first word.

Print each group on a separate line, with words in the group separated by a single space.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of words.
The second line contains N space-separated strings.
output_format: Print each sorted anagram group on a new line, space-separated, with groups ordered alphabetically by their first word.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^4
1 <= |word| <= 50
Total characters <= 10^5
Strings consist of lowercase English letters.
explanation:
- "act", "cat", and "tac" are anagrams. Alphabetically sorted: ["act", "cat", "tac"].
- "dog" and "god" are anagrams. Alphabetically sorted: ["dog", "god"].
Comparing first words "act" < "dog", so "act cat tac" is printed first.

test_cases.input:
6
rat tar art stop pots tops
test_cases.expected_output:
art rat tar
pots stop tops

edge_cases.explanation: Duplicate identical words clustered into single group.
All single character words forming singleton groups.

reference_solution_python:
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

def solve():
    raw = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not raw:
        return
    N = int(raw[0])
    words = raw[1:N+1]
    
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for w in words:
        key = ''.join(sorted(w))
        groups[key].append(w)
        
    result_groups = []
    for grp in groups.values():
        grp.sort()
        result_groups.append(grp)
        
    result_groups.sort(key=lambda g: g[0])
    
    for g in result_groups:
        print(' '.join(g))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()
time_complexity: O(N * L log L + N log N) where L is max word length

title: Mission Control Communication Directory Dynamic Autocomplete
problem_statement:
A space exploration ground control center operates an emergency radio directory. As an operator types the callsign prefix of a station character-by-character, the communication terminal dynamically displays all registered station names matching that prefix in alphabetical order.

Given a contact list of N station names (which may contain duplicates) and a query string S of length M:
For each prefix of S of length i (from 1 to M):
- Output all unique contact names starting with S[0..i-1], sorted in lexicographical order, separated by a single space.
- If no registered contact shares that prefix, print `0`.

Print each prefix's match results on a new line.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer N, the number of contact names.
The second line contains N space-separated strings representing the contacts.
The third line contains the query string S.
output_format: Print M lines. The i-th line contains the space-separated sorted unique contacts matching prefix of length i, or 0 if no match exists.
constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000
1 <= |contact| <= 50
1 <= |S| <= 50
All strings consist of lowercase English letters.
explanation:
- Prefix "g": Matches "g", "gee", "gkk" (sorted: "g gee gkk").
- Prefix "ge": Matches "gee".

test_cases.expected_output:
apollo apollo11 apollo13 aries
apollo apollo11 apollo13

edge_cases.explanation: Duplicate contacts in input directory deduplicated to single entry per prefix.
Mismatch at fourth character transitions to 0.

title: Hardware FPGA Register Array Binary Configuration Row Deduplication
problem_statement:
An embedded FPGA hardware accelerator configures a programmable switch with a boolean matrix of dimensions R x C containing bit flags (0s and 1s). Redundant duplicate configuration rows consume unnecessary logic block lookup tables and must be removed.

Using a binary Trie with children for bit 0 and bit 1, filter and print only the unique rows of the matrix in the order of their first appearance.

Print each unique row on a separate line, with its C binary values separated by a single space.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers R and C, the number of rows and columns.
The following R lines each contain C space-separated binary integers (0 or 1).
output_format: Print each unique row on a new line with space-separated values, preserving original encounter order.
constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 1000
R * C <= 2 * 10^5
Matrix cells contain either 0 or 1.
explanation:
Row 0: 0 1 0 0 (unique, outputted)
Row 1: 1 0 1 1 (unique, outputted)
Row 2: 0 1 0 0 (duplicate of row 0, omitted)
Row 3: 1 1 1 0 (unique, outputted)
